To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the hadronic freeze-out is a continuous process that is not well defined in time and space and (2) the freeze-out hypersurface is a smooth surface, which is determined by the local conditions in the hadronic matter, and not by the initial conditions of the reaction or the properties of the QGP.
the hadronic freeze-out is not a simple process, but a complicated one, that involves the collective motion of the hadrons.
the hadronic freeze-out is strongly influenced by the collective flow of the hadronic gas, and that the hadronic flow can be understood in terms of the collective expansion of the QGP phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics of bulk QCD matter created in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
the dynamics of hot and dense matter, which is created in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
the study of the properties of the hot and dense QCD medium, which is expected at RHIC and LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combined approach of relativistic hydrodynamical evolution of the QGP and microscopic hadronic evolution of the hadron gas is able to describe all experimental data available for the reaction system Au+Au at the RHIC.
the hydrodynamic model is a very powerful tool for the study of the reaction dynamics and the freeze-out properties of the system.

, in spite of the fact that there is no unique solution for the problem of the hadronic freeze-out in the context of a combined hydrodynamic+hadronic cascade approach, the results of our analysis indicate that a hadronization hypersur-face which is close to the surface of constant temperature T = 160 MeV, and a hadronization time of tau(freeze-out) = 8-12 fm/c, are in good agreement with the available data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is the first time that the freeze-out of hot QCD matter has been calculated in a self-consistent manner.
it is possible to describe the dynamics of hot bulk QCD matter from the quark-gluon plasma to hadronic freeze-out in a consistent way.

the combined hydrodynamic+UrQMD model is a promising approach for a consistent description of the whole reaction dynamics of relativistic nuclear collisions, from the early QGP phase to hadronic freeze-out.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hadronic freeze-out hypersurface is determined by the hydrodynamical evolution of the QGP, and that this hypersurface is not a simple freeze-out temperature surface, as is often assumed.

the freeze-out of a hadron resonance gas can be understood in a unified picture, where the freeze-out hypersurface is determined by the hadronization of the quark-gluon plasma, and the freeze-out temperature and the transverse flow are determined by the collective flow on this surface.
the hadronic freeze-out hypersurface can be calculated self-consistently, without introducing any phenomenological parameters or assumptions about the reaction dynamics.
